record.title: The leafless-graph upper-bound conjecture for edge metric dimension
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Its **edge metric dimension** is denoted by $\mathrm{edim}(G)$, its **cyclomatic number** by $c(G)=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1$, and $L(G)$ is the sum of the excess numbers of threads hanging at vertices. A graph is **leafless** when its minimum degree satisfies $\delta(G)\geq2$.

**Leafless-graph upper-bound conjecture.** Every leafless graph satisfies

$$
\mathrm{edim}(G)\leq 2c(G)-1.
$$

The paper proves this decreased bound for leafless cacti and for graphs with minimum degree at least three. Together with the analogous vertex statement, it is proposed as the sharp replacement for the earlier bound involving $L(G)$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Metric dimensions vs. cyclomatic number of graphs with minimum degree at least two”, arXiv:2108.09573 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09573

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2021). “As a first step towards the solution of this conjecture, we show that it holds for all graphs with $\delta(G)\geq3$.”

record.title: Super-exponential growth of minimal-origami orbits
record.statement: Let $N_g$ denote the number of distinct $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbits of origamis in $\mathcal{H}(2g-2)$ with $2g-1$ squares, such that each of their horizontal and vertical cylinder decompositions consists of one cylinder. **Super-exponential orbit-growth conjecture.** The quantity $N_g$ grows super-exponentially in $g$. These origamis, called minimal origamis, have the simplest possible horizontal and vertical cylinder decompositions and the smallest possible number of squares. The conjecture predicts that the number of distinct $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbits among them becomes extremely large as the genus grows, although the paper notes that even monotonicity in $g$ is unknown.
record.source_name: Tarik Aougab, William Menasco and Mark Nieland, “Origamis associated to minimally intersecting filling pairs”, arXiv:2108.10268 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10268

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: The multiplicative 1-2-3 Conjecture for multiset-proper edge-labellings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A graph is **nice** if none of its connected components is isomorphic to $K_2$, and let $\chi_{\rm M}(G)$ be the smallest $k\geq 1$ for which $G$ has an m-proper $k$-labelling, meaning an edge-labelling from $\{1,\dots,k\}$ whose incident-label multisets give different values at the ends of every edge.

**The multiplicative 1-2-3 Conjecture for multisets.** If $G$ is a nice graph, then

$$
\chi_{\rm M}(G)\leq 3.
$$

This is the multiset counterpart of the original 1-2-3 Conjecture, raised by Addario-Berry, Aldred, Dalal and Reed. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied material.
record.source_name: Julien Bensmail, Hervé Hocquard, Dimitri Lajou and Éric Sopena, “A proof of the Multiplicative 1-2-3 Conjecture”, arXiv:2108.10554 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10554

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: Equivariant Segal–Stolz–Teichner conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a symmetry group, let $
u$ be the gravitational anomaly, and let $k$ be the 't Hooft anomaly, with $
u\oplus k\in (I_\mathbb{Z}\Omega^	ext{spin})^4(BG)$. For a simple simply-connected compact Lie group, the non-gravitational part is identified with $\mathrm{H}^4(BG,\mathbb{Z})\simeq\mathbb{Z}$. **Equivariant Segal–Stolz–Teichner conjecture.** The equivariant $\mathrm{TMF}$ group $\mathrm{TMF}^{-(
u\oplus k)}_G(\mathrm{pt})$ is the deformation class of 2d $\mathcal{N}=(0,1)$ supersymmetric theories with anomaly $
u\oplus k\in (I_\mathbb{Z}\Omega^	ext{spin})^4(BG)$. This extends the proposed $\mathrm{TMF}$ classification from theories without symmetry to theories with a symmetry group and is intended to determine the anomaly of the corresponding spacetime theory.
record.source_name: Yuji Tachikawa and Mayuko Yamashita, “Topological modular forms and the absence of all heterotic global anomalies”, arXiv:2108.13542 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.13542

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: The zero-axis conjecture for dual objects of Loosened Collatz cycles
record.statement: Let a satisfying cycle determine its dual object in Euclidean space by interpreting its associated tuple and its bitwise rotations as vertices in $\mathbb{R}^n$. A vertex is said to be **zero on an axis** when at least one of its coordinates is $0$. **Zero-axis conjecture.** Excluding the point $(2,2,\ldots)$, all dual objects of satisfying cycles require their vertices to be $0$ on at least one axis. The source presents this as equivalent to the preceding tuple conjecture and gives no resolution, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Q Le and Edward Smith, “Observations on cycles in a variant of the Collatz Graph”, arXiv:2109.01180 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.01180

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Conjecture F for fibrations with split fibres away from a finite locus
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a number field. Let $\pi\in{\mathscr P}$ determine a variety $W$ and a smooth morphism $p:W\to {\mathbf P}^1_k$, with split fibres above $U={\mathbf P}^1_k\setminus M$. For $c\in {\mathbf P}^1_k$, write $W_c=p^{-1}(c)$.

**Conjecture F.** The subset

$$
\bigcup_{c\in U(k)}W_c({\mathbf A}_k)
$$

is dense in $W({\mathbf A}_k)$.

This is an arithmetic conjecture concerning adelic points on fibrations over the projective line, equivalent to Conjecture 9.1 of the cited work. Its status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Yonatan Harpaz, Dasheng Wei and Olivier Wittenberg, “Rational points on fibrations with few non-split fibres”, arXiv:2109.03547 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03547

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: The edge-deletion conjecture for graphs of odd chromatic index four
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $4_o'(G)$ denote its odd chromatic index, the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring whose color classes induce odd subgraphs of $G$.

**Edge-deletion conjecture.** If $4_o'(G)=4$, then there is an edge $e$ such that $G-e$ admits an odd $3$-edge-coloring.

This conjecture is related to the open question of whether every connected graph with odd chromatic index four admits an odd $4$-edge-coloring with a color class of size $1$.
record.source_name: Mirko Petruševski and Riste Škrekovski, “Odd edge-colorings of subdivisions of odd graphs”, arXiv:2109.04099 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.04099

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: The minimal edge-deletion example for strong I-contractibility
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $N(\{v,w\})$ denote the common neighborhood of an edge $\{v,w\}$, and let $\mathfrak{I}_S$ denote the class of $\mathfrak{I}_S$-contractible graphs. **The minimal edge-deletion example conjecture.** The graph depicted in Figure is the smallest graph, by number of vertices, satisfying both: $G$ is strong $\mathfrak{I}$-contractible; and there is an edge $\{v,w\}$ in $G$ such that $N(\{v,w\})\in\mathfrak{I}_S$ while $G\backslash\{v,w\}$ is not strong $\mathfrak{I}$-contractible. The conjecture concerns the minimality of the displayed computational example; no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Anton Dochtermann, Jesús F. Espinoza, Martín Eduardo Frías-Armenta and Héctor Alfredo Hernández-Hernández, “Minimal graphs for contractible and dismantlable properties”, arXiv:2109.06729 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06729

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2021). “Our next collection of open questions address the connection between the classes of graphs $\SVIC$, $\SIC$, and $\II$, and topological properties of their clique complexes.”

record.title: Gang–Kim–Yoon's norm-curve vanishing conjecture for adjoint Reidemeister torsions
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented compact hyperbolic $3$-manifold with a torus boundary. A **norm curve** is a one-dimensional component of the character variety on which every trace function is non-constant; write $X^{\mathrm{nor}}(M)$ for the set of all norm curves. For a slope $\gamma\in H_1(\partial M,\mathbb Z)$, let $\operatorname{tr}\rho(\gamma)$ be the trace of $\rho(\gamma)$ and let $\mathbb T_{M,\gamma}$ be the adjoint Reidemeister torsion. **Modified Gang–Kim–Yoon conjecture.** For generic $z\in\mathbb C$, 

$$
\sum_{\substack{[\rho]\in X^{\mathrm{nor}}(M)\\ \operatorname{tr}\rho(\gamma)=z}}\frac{1}{\mathbb T_{M,\gamma}}=0.
$$

The modification excludes extra character-variety components containing constant trace functions. The paper shows that this identity holds for all hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundles with tunnel number one, although its validity in the stated generality remains open.
record.source_name: Anh T. Tran and Yoshikazu Yamaguchi, “Adjoint Reidemeister torsions of once-punctured torus bundles”, arXiv:2109.07058 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.07058

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Continuous Zauner's conjecture for equiangular tight continuous frames
record.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $d\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\{\tau_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Omega}$ be a continuous frame for the Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$. The frame is **$\gamma$-equiangular** if there exists $\gamma\geq 0$ such that

$$
|\langle\tau_\alpha,\tau_\beta\rangle|=\gamma,\qquad \forall\alpha,\beta\in\Omega,\ \alpha\neq\beta.
$$

It is **tight** if its frame operator is a scalar multiple of the identity. **Continuous Zauner's conjecture.** For a given measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and for every $d\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a $\gamma$-equiangular tight continuous frame $\{\tau_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Omega}$ for $\mathbb{C}^d$ such that $\mu(\Omega)=d^2$. This is the continuous analogue of Zauner's conjecture for equiangular tight frames; the existence assertion is posed for every dimension and measure space, and its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: K. Mahesh Krishna, “Continuous Welch bounds with Applications”, arXiv:2109.09296 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09296

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: The Plücker-coordinate volume relation for polytopes
record.statement:
Let $G(n-d,n)$ denote the Grassmannian of $(n-d)$-dimensional subspaces of an $n$-dimensional space, and let $\bm{p}$ be a Plücker-coordinate vector in $\bigcup\limits_n G(n-d,n)$. Let $V$ be the volume of the corresponding polytope. **Plücker-coordinate volume conjecture.** There exists a map

$$
f:\bigcup\limits_n G(n-d,n)\rightarrow\mathbb{R},\qquad \bm{p}\mapsto x
$$

such that

$$
V\sim |x|+1,
$$

where $1$ indicates the smallest normalized volume among the polytopes. This conjecture proposes a simple one-dimensional relation between Plücker-coordinate data and polytope volume, motivated by the observed one-component multidimensional-scaling projections; the supplied text gives no evidence that the relation has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Jiakang Bao, Yang-Hui He, Edward Hirst, Johannes Hofscheier, Alexander Kasprzyk and Suvajit Majumder, “Polytopes and Machine Learning”, arXiv:2109.09602 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for maximal entries in the associated solution tree
record.statement: Let $\mathbb T$ be the tree constructed from positive integer solutions of the paper's Diophantine equation, and let $(x,y,z)$ be a positive integer solution of that equation. The **maximal number** of a solution is the largest of its three coordinates. **Uniqueness conjecture for the associated tree.** Every number appearing in the tree $\mathbb T$ appears exactly once as the maximal number of some positive integer solution to the Diophantine equation. The statement is presented as a conjecture parallel to Markov's uniqueness conjecture; the supplied text does not establish its status, so it is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Yasuaki Gyoda, “Positive integer solutions to (x+y)^2+(y+z)^2+(z+x)^2=12xyz”, arXiv:2109.09639 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09639

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2021). “In addition, the Markov Diophantine equation has the following famous open problem.”

record.title: Revised Vallentin conjecture for distance-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a distance-regular graph with diameter $d$, with eigenvalues $\theta_0>\theta_1>\cdots>\theta_d$ and cosine sequences $(w_0(\theta_j),\ldots,w_d(\theta_j))$ corresponding to the eigenvalues. Let $c_2(G)$ denote the least Euclidean distortion of the shortest-path metric of $G$. **Revised Vallentin conjecture.**

$$
c_2(G)^2=\max_{r\in\{d-1,d\}}\left\{r^2\frac{1-w_1(\theta_1)}{1-w_r(\theta_1)}\right\}.
$$

The maximum occurs at $r=d$ unless $G$ is antipodal. The paper proves this revised conjecture for diameter $3$ and gives partial results for diameter $4$.
record.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioabă, Himanshu Gupta, Ferdinand Ihringer and Hirotake Kurihara, “The least Euclidean distortion constant of a distance-regular graph”, arXiv:2109.09708 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09708

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Endpoint minimum conjecture for cosine sequences of distance-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a distance-regular graph of diameter $d$ with eigenvalues $\theta_0>\theta_1>\cdots>\theta_d$. For the cosine sequence $(w_0(\theta_1),w_1(\theta_1),\ldots,w_d(\theta_1))$ of $\theta_1$, **endpoint minimum conjecture.**

$$
\min_{1\leq r\leq d}\left\{\frac{1-w_r(\theta_1)}{r^2}\right\}=\min_{r\in\{d-1,d\}}\left\{\frac{1-w_r(\theta_1)}{r^2}\right\}.
$$

The minimum occurs at $r=d$ unless $G$ is antipodal. This conjecture is proposed as one of two auxiliary conjectures supporting the revised Vallentin conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioabă, Himanshu Gupta, Ferdinand Ihringer and Hirotake Kurihara, “The least Euclidean distortion constant of a distance-regular graph”, arXiv:2109.09708 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09708

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Hurajová-Coroničová–Madaras diameter conjecture for betweenness-uniform graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a betweenness-uniform graph, let $n$ be its number of vertices, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $d(G)$ denote its diameter. Suppose that

$$
\Delta(G)=n-k.
$$

**Hurajová-Coroničová–Madaras conjecture.** Then

$$
d(G)\leq k.
$$

This conjecture concerns how the maximum degree constrains the diameter of betweenness-uniform graphs. The source paper states that it proves the conjecture, so the claim is resolved.
record.source_name: David Hartman, Aneta Pokorná and Pavel Valtr, “On the Connectivity and the Diameter of Betweenness-Uniform Graphs”, arXiv:2109.10594 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10594

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Conjecture on the ordered continued-fraction coefficients of quadratic integers
record.statement:
Let

$$
\Delta=[\overline{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{l-1}}]
$$

be a purely periodic quadratic integer, and let $\mathcal{C}(\Delta)=\\{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{l-1}\\}$. For each positive integer $n$, let $w_n$ be the $n$-th largest element of $\mathcal{C}(\Delta)$. **Quadratic-integer coefficient conjecture.** The ordered coefficients satisfy

$$
w_n\leq\frac{a_0}{n}.
$$

The conjecture proposes quantitative control of all continued fraction coefficients of a purely periodic quadratic integer. The preceding corollary establishes only the bound $a_i\leq a_0$ for the coefficients of $\sqrt d$; the stronger assertion for general purely periodic quadratic integers is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Thomas Lachmann and Jaspar Wiart, “On the area of empty axis-parallel rectangles amidst 2-dimensional lattice points”, arXiv:2109.11222 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.11222

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: The subgraph core conjecture for connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For each vertex $v\in V(G)$, let $f_G(v)$ be the number of connected subgraphs of $G$ containing $v$, and let $S_c(G)$ be the set of vertices with maximum subgraph number, called the **subgraph core** of $G$.

**Subgraph core conjecture.** The subgraph core of $G$ is contained in a block of $G$.

This conjecture extends the known property that central parts of graphs lie in a block. For trees, the subgraph core is already known to consist of either one vertex or two adjacent vertices; the asserted containment in a block is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Dinesh Pandey and Kamal Lochan Patra, “Some new central parts of connected graphs”, arXiv:2110.00738 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00738

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Ghosh–Győri–Martin–Paulos–Xiao conjecture on planar Turán numbers of cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_{\ell}$ denote the cycle of length $\ell$, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_{\ell})$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no copy of $C_{\ell}$. For each $\ell\ge 7$, and for sufficiently large $n$, every such graph $G$ satisfies

$$
e(G)\le \frac{3(\ell-1)}{\ell}n-\frac{6(\ell+1)}{\ell}.
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_{\ell})\le \frac{3(\ell-1)}{\ell}n-\frac{6(\ell+1)}{\ell}.
$$

This conjecture is the bound proposed by Ghosh, Győri, Martin, Paulos, and Xiao for planar Turán numbers of cycles of length at least seven; the paper disproves it.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, Bernard Lidický, Xiaonan Liu and Abhinav Shantanam, “Planar Turán Numbers of Cycles: A Counterexample”, arXiv:2110.02043 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.02043

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Set-wise intersection conjecture for perfect matchings
record.statement:
Let $K_{2k}$ be the complete graph on $2k$ vertices. For $t\leq \lfloor k/2\rfloor$, two perfect matchings are **set-wise $t$-intersecting** if some $t$ edges in each matching cover the same set of vertices. A family is set-wise $t$-intersecting if every pair of its members is set-wise $t$-intersecting.

**Set-wise intersection conjecture.** For $k\geq 2t$, the largest set-wise $t$-intersecting family of perfect matchings in $K_{2k}$ has size

$$
(2t-1)!!(2k-2t-1)!!.
$$

Moreover, every maximum-size family is an orbit of the Young subgroup $Sym(2t)\times Sym(2k-2t)$.

This conjecture extends the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem from ordinary intersection to set-wise intersection. The paper proves the corresponding result for $t=2$; the cases $t\geq 3$ remain open.
record.source_name: Mahsa N. Shirazi, “An extension of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem to set-wise 2-intersecting families of perfect matchings”, arXiv:2110.02175 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.02175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Gir\~ao, Popielarz, and Snyder's oriented Ramsey conjecture for 1-subdivisions
record.statement:
Let $T_k$ be the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices, and let $H_k$ be its $1$-subdivision, obtained by subdividing every arc exactly once. For an oriented graph $H$, let $\vec{r}(H)$ be the smallest integer $n$ such that every $n$-vertex tournament contains a copy of $H$. **Gir\~ao, Popielarz, and Snyder's conjecture.** The oriented Ramsey number of $H_k$ satisfies

$$
\vec{r}(H_k)=O(k^2).
$$

Previously, the bound $\vec{r}(H_k)=O(k^2\log^3 k)$ was known; the conjecture asks whether the logarithmic factor can be removed.
record.source_name: Jaehoon Kim, Hyunwoo Lee and Jaehyeon Seo, “On 1-subdivisions of transitive tournaments”, arXiv:2110.05002 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05002

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: The genus-square-root conjecture for proper chromatic number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph embedded on an orientable surface of genus $g$. A **proper orientation** is an orientation in which adjacent vertices have different outdegrees, and the **proper chromatic number** $\Vec{\chi}(G)$ is the minimum possible maximum outdegree over all proper orientations of $G$.

**Genus-square-root conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph of genus $g$, then

$$
\Vec{\chi}(G)\le O(g^{1/2}).
$$

The paper previously obtains the weaker bound $O(g^{1/2}\log g/\log\log g)$ and proposes this conjecture as a possible improvement; the sharper square-root bound remains open.
record.source_name: Yaobin Chen, Bojan Mohar and Hehui Wu, “Proper orientations and proper chromatic number”, arXiv:2110.07005 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07005

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Canonical-subspace conjecture for maximum cliques in semi-primitive pseudo-Paley graphs
record.statement:
Let $X=PP(q,2d,I)$ be a semi-primitive pseudo-Paley graph with $q=p^{2rt}$, where $r$ is even. A maximum clique is a clique of size $\omega(X)$. **Canonical-subspace conjecture.** If

$$
\omega(X)=\sqrt{q},
$$

then every maximum clique in $X$ is an $\mathbb{F}_{p^t}$-affine subspace. This conjecture extends the known $\mathbb{F}_p$-subspace structure in the odd-$r$ case and asserts that square-root maximum cliques in the even-$r$ case have the corresponding canonical subfield structure. The source presents this as open.
record.source_name: Shamil Asgarli and Chi Hoi Yip, “The subspace structure of maximum cliques in pseudo-Paley graphs from unions of cyclotomic classes”, arXiv:2110.07176 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Two-clique conjecture for square-root maximum cliques
record.statement:
Let $X=PP(q,2d,I)$ be a semi-primitive pseudo-Paley graph with $q=p^{2rt}$, where $r$ is even, and assume

$$
0\in I,\qquad I\ne\{0,2,\ldots,2d-2\}.
$$

A maximum clique is a clique of size $\omega(X)$. **Two-clique conjecture.** If

$$
\omega(X)=\sqrt{q},
$$

then exactly two maximum cliques in $X$ contain $\mathbb{F}_{p^t}$. This conjecture strengthens and generalizes the theorem discussed immediately before it, and the source presents it as an open conjecture motivated by computational examples.
record.source_name: Shamil Asgarli and Chi Hoi Yip, “The subspace structure of maximum cliques in pseudo-Paley graphs from unions of cyclotomic classes”, arXiv:2110.07176 (2024).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Infinite-family conjecture for non-Paley pseudo-Paley graphs
record.statement:
For a prime $p\geq 3$, consider subsets $I\subset\{0,1,\ldots,p\}$ with $0\in I$ and $|I|=(p+1)/2$, and the associated graph $PP(p^4,p+1,I)$. Let $g$ be the primitive element used to define the cyclotomic classes. **Infinite-family conjecture.** For each prime $p\geq 3$, exactly

$$
\frac{p^2+3}{4}
$$

such subsets $I$ satisfy

$$
\omega\bigl(PP(p^4,p+1,I)\bigr)=p^2.
$$

Furthermore, in these graphs, every maximum clique containing $\{0,1\}$ is of the form

$$
\mathbb{F}_p\oplus a\mathbb{F}_p,
$$

where $a=g^{(p+1)k}$ and $k$ is an odd integer. The conjecture is motivated by the expectation of infinitely many non-Paley examples, while the source notes that direct verification is impractical and introduces a weaker conjecture for computational testing.
record.source_name: Shamil Asgarli and Chi Hoi Yip, “The subspace structure of maximum cliques in pseudo-Paley graphs from unions of cyclotomic classes”, arXiv:2110.07176 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Savery's extremal conjecture for induced cycles in planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $f_I(n,C_k)$ denote the maximum number of induced copies of the cycle $C_k$ in an $n$-vertex planar graph. Let $F_{n,k}$ be the planar graph obtained by blowing up three pairwise non-adjacent vertices of a $k$-cycle into vertex classes of as equal size as possible, as defined in the paper. **Savery's conjecture.** For $k\geq 6$ and $n$ sufficiently large relative to $k$, the graph $F_{n,k}$ contains

$$
f_I(n,C_k)
$$

induced $k$-cycles; equivalently, $F_{n,k}$ is extremal for this problem. The conjecture concerns odd cycles of length greater than five in particular, and the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Michael Savery, “Planar graphs with the maximum number of induced 6-cycles”, arXiv:2110.07319 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07319

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: The polynomial bound conjecture for intersecting subsets of the affine general linear group
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $\AGL(2,q)$ act on the affine plane, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\AGL(2,q)$ be **intersecting**, meaning that any two elements of $\mathcal{F}$ agree on at least one point. **Polynomial bound conjecture.** There exist $a\in\mathbb{N}$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq q^2(q-1)(aq+b).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the maximum intersecting sets in $\AGL(2,q)$ have a substantially smaller order than the general upper bound known from the ratio method. The source provides constructions and bounds but no resolution of this assertion.
record.source_name: Karen Meagher and A. Sarobidy Razafimahatratra, “Erdős-Ko-Rado results for the general linear group, the special linear group and the affine general linear group”, arXiv:2110.08972 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.08972

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Uniform Fitting-height conjecture for fixed-point-free automorphisms satisfying polynomial identities
record.statement:
Let $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]\setminus\{0\}$. An automorphism $\alpha$ of a finite group $G$ has **ordered identity** $f(x)$ if the corresponding identity in the group ring holds for $\alpha$; it is **fixed-point-free** if $C_G(\alpha)=1$. The **Fitting height** of a finite solvable group is the length of its Fitting series.

**Uniform Fitting-height conjecture.** For every $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]\setminus\{0\}$, there exist integers $k(f(x))>0$ and $m(f(x))$ such that, whenever $G$ is a finite solvable group admitting a fixed-point-free automorphism $\alpha$ for which $f(x)$ is an ordered identity, the following hold: (a) the Fitting height of $G$ is at most $m(f(x))$; and (b) if $\gcd(|G|,k(f(x)))=1$, then the Fitting height of $G$ is at most the number of irreducible factors of $f(x)$.

The conjecture seeks a uniform bound depending only on the polynomial identity, with a sharper bound after excluding finitely many primes from $|G|$. It is motivated by results of Thompson, Berger, Turull and others on Fitting height under fixed-point-free automorphisms, but the stated uniform bounds are presented here as a conjecture.

record.title: Rolland Rigidity conjecture for self-diffeomorphisms of locally symmetric spaces
record.statement:
Suppose $M$ is a locally symmetric space with natural Riemannian metric $\rho$ and Levi-Civita connection $
abla$. Let $f$ be a self-diffeomorphism of $M$, and let $(g_{1,b})$ and $(g_{2,b})$ be distinct smooth root systems to the identity inducing distinct vector fields $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$. **Rolland Rigidity conjecture.** There is a class of such self-diffeomorphisms for which, for every $p\in M$, the points $p$ and $f(p)$ are conjugate with respect to $
abla$. For each self-diffeomorphism in this class, there should be a differential equation $\xi_b$ on $M$, positive integers $k_1,k_2$, and inversion symmetries $P_1,P_2$ of $(M,\rho)$ satisfying

$$
k_iDP_i\circ\xi_c=\xi_i\circ P_i.
$$

Here $DP_i:TM\to TM$ is the induced map on the tangent bundle. If $
abla$ is nonpositively curved, then $(M,\nabla)$ has no conjugate points, and every self-diffeomorphism in this class should induce a unique differential equation $\xi$ and hence a necessarily unique flow $\Phi_t$ with

$$
f=\Phi_{t=1}.
$$

The claim proposes a rigidity phenomenon determined by $f$, with the base differential equation $\xi_b$ serving as part of that structure. Its status is unclear from the supplied text; the source presents it as a suspicion rather than establishing it as a theorem.
record.source_name: Jeffrey J. Rolland, “A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for a Self-Diffeomorphism of a Smooth Manifold to be the Time-1 Map of the Flow of a Differential Equation”, arXiv:2110.12806 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.12806

record.title: Positivity conjecture for Sylow branching coefficients of powers of two
record.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\lambda\vdash 2^k$. Write $l(\lambda)$ for the number of parts of $\lambda$, let $\lambda_{l(\lambda)}$ be its smallest part, and let $Z^\lambda$ be the Sylow branching coefficient defined in the source. **Sylow branching positivity conjecture.** If $\lambda_{l(\lambda)}\ge 2$, then

$$
Z^\lambda>0
$$

unless $\lambda=(5,3)$, or $k\ge 3$ and $\lambda=(3,3,2^{2^{k-1}-3})$. This conjecture gives a proposed classification of the exceptional zero Sylow branching coefficients in the stated family; the source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Stacey Law and Yuji Okitani, “On plethysms and Sylow branching coefficients”, arXiv:2110.14552 (2022).

record.title: Minimal-clique-cover conjecture for realizable graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a realizable graph. A **clique cover** of $H$ is a collection of cliques whose union covers all edges of $H$, and let $n$ be the smallest number of cliques in such a cover. **Minimal-clique-cover conjecture.** There is always a digraph $G$ realizing $H$ with

$$
|V_G|=n.
$$

Equivalently, the theorem characterizing realizability continues to hold when the number of cliques is required to be minimal. This would make the decidability algorithm substantially more efficient by restricting the search to minimum-size clique covers; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: J. Fromentin, P. -L Giscard and T. Karaboghossian, “Realizable cycle structures in digraphs”, arXiv:2110.15618 (2023).

record.title: Beaton–Brown conjecture on the modes of domination polynomials of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree and let $v\in V(T)$ be a leaf. Let $D(T)$ and $D(T\backslash v)$ denote the domination polynomials of $T$ and the tree obtained by deleting $v$, respectively. Assume that both polynomials are unimodal, and let their modes be the largest indices at which their coefficient sequences attain the required increase-then-decrease transition. **Beaton–Brown's conjecture.** The modes of $D(T)$ and $D(T\backslash v)$ are at distance at most $1$.

This conjecture proposes a local stability property for domination-polynomial modes under deletion of a leaf. The source presents it as an open direction for graphs such as trees, where the paper's techniques do not resolve unimodality in general.
record.source_name: Shengtong Zhang, “Domination polynomial is unimodal for large graphs with a universal vertex”, arXiv:2111.00641 (2021).

record.title: Existence of codes with closed embedding dimension exceeding base set size
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\operatorname{cdim}(\mathcal C)$ denote the closed embedding dimension of a code $\mathcal C\subseteq 2^{[n]}$. **Closed-dimension existence conjecture.** There exists a code $\mathcal C\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ such that

$$
n<\operatorname{cdim}(\mathcal C)<\infty.
$$

The paper notes that no such example was known there, despite analogous open embedding dimensions being able to exceed $n$; finding one would provide a starting point for understanding the minimum base set size needed for a prescribed closed embedding dimension.

record.title: Conjecture on the secrecy gain of formally unimodular lattices
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a formally unimodular lattice, with secrecy function $\Xi_{\Lambda}(\tau)$, and denote its secrecy gain by $\xi_{\Lambda}$. **Formally unimodular secrecy-gain conjecture.** The secrecy function of $\Lambda$ achieves its maximum at $\tau=1$, namely

$$
\xi_{\Lambda}=\Xi_{\Lambda}(1).
$$

The conjecture concerns whether the symmetry point remains the maximizing point for formally unimodular lattices, extending the preceding question beyond unimodular lattices; the source gives no resolution status.

record.title: The disjoint-edge bound for geometric graphs
record.statement:
Let $m$ be a non-negative integer and $G$ be a geometric graph such that $|DJ(uv)|\leq m$ for any edge $uv\in E(G)$. **The disjoint-edge bound.** Then

$$
|E(G)|\leq \frac{\sqrt{1+8m}+3}{4}\cdot |V(G)|.
$$

The conjecture proposes a sharp-looking linear bound on the number of edges in terms of the maximum number of edges disjoint from an individual edge. The source gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.

record.title: Minimal-model conjecture under LSA
record.statement: Assume $AD^+$ and that there is a largest Suslin cardinal which is a member of the Solovay sequence. A transitive model $M$ of $ZF$ is a **minimal model of $\Theta strong$** when $Ord\cup\mathbb{R}\subseteq M$, $M\vDash\Theta strong$, and every transitive proper submodel $N\subsetneq M$ containing $Ord\cup\mathbb{R}$ satisfies $N\vDash\neg\Theta strong$. Here $\Theta strong$ denotes $AD_{\mathbb{R}}$ together with the assertion that $\Theta$ is a strong cardinal. **Conditional minimal-model conjecture.** There is a minimal model of $\Theta strong$. The hypothesis is known as LSA and is stated in the source to be consistent relative to a Woodin cardinal that is itself a limit of Woodin cardinals; the conditional existence claim remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: LSA conjecture for a strong-cardinal model with a Woodin cardinal
record.statement: Let $LSA$ abbreviate the assertion that $AD^+$ holds and there is a largest Suslin cardinal belonging to the Solovay sequence. Let $\vec{E}$ be an extender sequence and write $L^{\vec{E}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}))$ for the corresponding extender model over the power set of the reals. **LSA model conjecture.** Assume $LSA$. Then there is a model $\mathcal{M}=L^{\vec{E}}(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}))$ of $AD_{\mathbb{R}}$ in which $\Theta$ is a strong cardinal and $\mathcal{M}\vDash$ “there is a Woodin cardinal”. The source presents this as a conjectural direction for the fine structure of models of LSA; no proof or resolution is given.

record.title: Minimum domination conjecture for the augmented Cartesian product
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $D_G$ and $D_H$ be minimum dominating sets of $G$ and $H$, respectively, and let $A_{G,H}[F_G,F_H]$ denote the graph obtained by the paper's edge-adjoining construction from the edge sets $F_G$ and $F_H$. The Cartesian product $D_G\times D_H$ is a dominating set in this augmented graph. **Minimum domination conjecture.** The set $D_G\times D_H$ is a minimum dominating set for

$$
A_{G,H}[F_G,F_H].
$$

The conjecture is the paper's proposed strengthening of the construction's minimality conclusion: it asserts that the dominating set of cardinality $\gamma(G)\gamma(H)$ is minimum, not merely minimal. The paper states that this conjecture would imply Vizing's conjecture.
record.source_name: Allan van Hulst, “Adjoining edges to GH to construct a minimal dominating set of size γ(G)γ(H)”, arXiv:2111.08371 (2021).

record.title: Cofiber Morava K-theory dimension formula conjecture for real Grassmannians
record.statement:
Let $C_d({\mathbb R}^m)$ be the cofiber of the inclusion $\operatorname{Gr}_d({\mathbb R}^{m-1})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}_d({\mathbb R}^m)$, and let $\bar k_n(C_d({\mathbb R}^m))$ denote its reduced Morava K-theory dimension. Let $n\geq 1$, let $\epsilon$ be $0$ or $1$, and let $l\geq 0$, with $m=2^{n+1}-\epsilon+2l$. **Cofiber Morava K-theory dimension formula conjecture.** Equality should hold in the proved lower bound, namely

$$
\bar k_n(C_d({\mathbb R}^m))=\sum_i\binom{2^{n+1}-1-\epsilon}{d-1-2i}\binom{l}{i}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by a corresponding calculation of the $Q_n$-homology of the cofiber and would determine the lower bound exactly. It remains open.
record.source_name: Nicholas J. Kuhn and Christopher J. R. Lloyd, “Computing the Morava K-theory of real Grassmanians using chromatic fixed point theory”, arXiv:2111.08812 (2021).

record.title: Classification conjecture for Sidon polynomials over prime fields
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $P\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ be a **Sidon polynomial**, meaning that $P$ parametrizes a Sidon set in the associated polynomial construction. For polynomials $P,P'\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$, write $P\sim_{\mathcal S}P'$ when

$$
P'=R\circ P\circ T
$$

for some permutation polynomials $R,T\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$.

**Sidon-polynomial classification conjecture.** If $P\in\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ is a Sidon polynomial, then either

$$
P\sim_{\mathcal S}x
$$

or

$$
P\sim_{\mathcal S}x^2.
$$

This is the reformulation of the maximum-Sidon-set classification in terms of Sidon-equivalence classes. The supplied source gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Morita equivalence of weakly and strictly stable weak identity types
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{CwF}_{ws}$ be the category of contextual categories with weakly stable weak identity types, let $I_{ws}$ be the corresponding generating cofibrations, and let $L$ be the left adjoint in the free-forgetful adjunction between weakly stable and strictly stable structures. For an $I_{ws}$-cellular model $\mathcal{C}:\mathbf{CwF}_{ws}$, write $\eta:\mathcal{C}\to L(\mathcal{C})$ for the unit.

**Morita equivalence conjecture.** The theories of weakly stable weak identity types and strictly stable weak identity types are Morita equivalent: for every $I_{ws}$-cellular model $\mathcal{C}:\mathbf{CwF}_{ws}$, the unit

$$
\eta:\mathcal{C}\to L(\mathcal{C})
$$

is a weak equivalence.

This would provide the desired coherence theorem by showing that strictification preserves the homotopical theory of weakly stable identity types. The paper presents this as a goal toward a full coherence theorem, and no proof or resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Rafaël Bocquet, “Strictification of weakly stable type-theoretic structures using generic contexts”, arXiv:2111.10862 (2022).
